narrative.intro: National Aeronautics and Space Administration obligated $1.2B on contracts in FY2027 to date. National Aeronautics and Space Administration issued 1,200 awards with an average award size of $987K. National Aeronautics and Space Administration obligations are down 92.6% year over year, reflecting that the current fiscal-year total is partial and far below recent full-year totals. National Aeronautics and Space Administration obligated $15.2B in FY22, $16.1B in FY23, $15B in FY24, $15.8B in FY25, and $16.1B in FY26. Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology) is the largest NAICS category in FY2027 to date at $487M. National Aeronautics and Space Administration also spent in Nonscheduled Chartered Freight Air Transportation ($176M), Guided Missile and Space Vehicle Manufacturing ($153M), and several other categories. CALIFORNIA INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY is the top vendor in FY2027 to date at $206M, followed by THE JOHNS HOPKINS UNIVERSITY APPLIED PHYSICS LABORATORY LLC at $132M and BLUE ORIGIN, LLC at $99.2M. The figures reflect contract obligations; the fiscal year is ongoing.

sections.heading: How has National Aeronautics and Space Administration contract spending changed in FY2027 to date?
sections.body: National Aeronautics and Space Administration obligated $1.2B in FY2027 to date. National Aeronautics and Space Administration obligations are down 92.6% year over year. National Aeronautics and Space Administration issued 1,200 awards with an average award size of $987K. National Aeronautics and Space Administration full fiscal-year obligations were $16.1B in FY26 and ranged from $15B to $16.1B in FY22 through FY26.

sections.heading: What did National Aeronautics and Space Administration buy in FY2027 to date?
sections.body: Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology) accounted for $487M of obligations. Nonscheduled Chartered Freight Air Transportation was $176M and Guided Missile and Space Vehicle Manufacturing was $153M. National Aeronautics and Space Administration also obligated funds for Industrial Building Construction ($34.8M), Facilities Support Services ($34.1M), and Engineering Services ($33.6M).

faq.q: How much does National Aeronautics and Space Administration spend on contracts?
faq.a: National Aeronautics and Space Administration obligated $1.2B on contracts in FY2027 to date. National Aeronautics and Space Administration issued 1,200 awards with an average award size of $987K, and the current-year total is partial. National Aeronautics and Space Administration obligations are down 92.6% year over year compared with the prior fiscal period.

faq.q: What does National Aeronautics and Space Administration buy?
faq.a: National Aeronautics and Space Administration buys research, transportation, manufacturing, construction, and services. Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology) totaled $487M, Nonscheduled Chartered Freight Air Transportation totaled $176M, and Guided Missile and Space Vehicle Manufacturing totaled $153M in FY2027 to date. National Aeronautics and Space Administration also bought Industrial Building Construction ($34.8M), Facilities Support Services ($34.1M), and Engineering Services ($33.6M), among other categories.

faq.q: Who are National Aeronautics and Space Administration's largest contractors?
faq.a: National Aeronautics and Space Administration's largest contractors by obligations in FY2027 to date are CALIFORNIA INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY ($206M), THE JOHNS HOPKINS UNIVERSITY APPLIED PHYSICS LABORATORY LLC ($132M), and BLUE ORIGIN, LLC ($99.2M). THE BOEING COMPANY is $91M, AEROJET ROCKETDYNE OF DE, INC is $53.4M, IMPULSE SPACE, INC. is $37.1M, LOCKHEED MARTIN CORP is $30M, ROCKET LAB USA INC is $28.9M, SOUTHWEST RESEARCH INSTITUTE is $26.1M, and HITT CONTRACTING, INC. is $22.9M.
